definitions.explanation: The act or state of going upward.
A train heading toward a major city (especially Tokyo).

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}は{上|のぼ}りがきつい。
examples.english: The climb on this road is steep.

examples.japanese: {上|のぼ}りの{電車|でんしゃ}は{混|こ}んでいる。
{上|のぼ}り{坂|ざか}で{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{漕|こ}ぐのは{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: It's hard to pedal a bicycle uphill.

examples.japanese: この{上|のぼ}りは{距離|きょり}が{長|なが}くて{疲|つか}れる。
examples.english: This uphill stretch is long and tiring.

examples.japanese: {上|のぼ}りと{下|くだ}りでは{所要|しょよう}{時間|じかん}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: The time needed differs between going up and coming down.

examples.japanese: {上|のぼ}りの{新幹線|しんかんせん}は{朝|あさ}が{混|こ}む。
examples.english: The inbound Shinkansen is crowded in the morning.

notes:
{上|のぼ}り is the noun form derived from the verb {上|のぼ}る (to climb, to go up).

TRAIN TERMINOLOGY:
In Japanese railway, {上|のぼ}り and {下|くだ}り indicate direction relative to major cities:
- {上|のぼ}り: toward Tokyo (or the major terminus)
- {下|くだ}り: away from Tokyo (or the major terminus)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {上|のぼ}り{坂|ざか} (uphill slope)
- {上|のぼ}り{線|せん} (inbound line/track)
- {上|のぼ}り{列車|れっしゃ} (up-train)

ANTONYM:
{下|くだ}り (descent; down-train)
